channel.title: Wandering Through God's Word with Wonder
channel.description: Daily Scripture reflections that invite you to slow down, linger, and wander through God's Word.
channel.itunes:author: Hope A Little
channel.itunes:summary: Daily Scripture reflections that invite you to slow down, linger, and wander through God's Word.

item.title: You Would Have No Authority Over Me
item.description: John 19:1-15 - Continuing the thread from Gethsemane and Jesus' arrest, this reflection sits with the contrast between how powerless Jesus appears and the authority He still possesses. Even while mocked, beaten, and moved steadily toward the cross, Jesus makes clear that Pilate's authority exists only because it has been given from above—and He continues willingly toward the sacrifice He came to make.

item.title: Who Do You Say Jesus Is?
item.description: John 18:28-40 - Surrounded by political tension and people trying to decide what to do with Him, Jesus remains completely clear about who He is and the kingdom He came to establish. Following Pilate's questions about kingship and truth, this reflection turns the question back toward us: does the Jesus we believe in actually line up with the Jesus who reveals Himself in Scripture?

item.title: When Jesus Doesn't Match Our Expectations
item.description: John 18:25-27 - Peter had been adamant that he would never deny Jesus, yet when events began unfolding in a way he may not have expected, he did exactly that. This reflection wonders whether Peter was experiencing a crisis of faith as the Jesus he thought he understood no longer seemed to match what was happening—and connects that tension to the moments when our own expectations of what God will do collide with reality.

item.title: He Spoke Openly
item.description: John 18:12-24 - Carrying forward the realization that Jesus entered His arrest with full authority and purpose, this reflection looks at His words before Annas in a different light—not as defensiveness, but as a reminder that He had never hidden who He was. Following Jesus' words back into Isaiah and then forward to Caiaphas' earlier prophecy, the reflection traces the way Jesus openly fulfills what had already been spoken about Him.

item.title: Authority and a Surrendered Heart
item.description: John 18:1-11 - As Jesus is arrested, He is not powerless or overtaken—He remains fully in authority, even while willingly surrendering to the Father's plan and protecting the disciples entrusted to Him. From there, this reflection follows the contrast between Judas and the other disciples: being close to Jesus is not the same as surrendering to Him, leaving us with the question of who or what truly has our heart.

item.title: The Glory He Has Given Us
item.description: John 17:22-26 - This reflection wrestles with the astonishing idea that some of what Jesus accomplished for us is not only a future promise—it has already been given. Sitting with Jesus' words about glory and Paul's words in Romans, it considers what it means to spend a lifetime learning to live in the victory, love, and new identity Christ has already made possible, rather than continually trying to earn what He has given.

item.title: Jesus Prayed for Us
item.description: John 17:1-21 - This reflection sits with the depth of Jesus' prayer and the things about Him that can feel almost too large to fully comprehend—from His existence before the world began to His relationship with the Father. Then comes an astonishingly personal realization: Jesus' prayer reaches beyond the disciples sitting with Him that night to those who would one day believe through their testimony—including us.

item.title: Where Peace Comes From
item.description: John 16:23-33 - This reflection follows a trail about peace—what it is, what it is not, and where it actually comes from. Rather than promising a life without trouble, Scripture repeatedly points us back to God: bringing our worries to Him, guarding what we allow our minds to dwell on, and learning to keep our focus on Jesus in the middle of a world that still brings tribulation.

item.title: When God Only Gives the Next Step
item.description: John 16:16-22 - This reflection follows the disciples as they try to understand a future that suddenly looks very different from what they expected—and connects that uncertainty to the moments when our own lives take an unexpected turn. It considers how God often gives us enough to take the next step rather than revealing the entire plan, using the waiting and uncertainty to shape who we are becoming while asking us to keep trusting Him.

item.title: When You Cannot Bear It Yet
item.description: John 16:1-15 - Jesus prepares His disciples for hardship with compassion, promising that although He is leaving, the Holy Spirit will come to guide, teach, and remain with them. He gives them enough to hold onto now, knowing they cannot bear everything at once, and reminds them that remembering His words will help steady them when hard things come.

item.title: The Cost of Following Jesus
item.description: John 15:18-27 - After speaking to His disciples about abiding, love, and friendship, Jesus changes the tone and prepares them for what following Him will also cost. He tells them plainly that the world that rejected and persecuted Him may reject them too, while reminding them that He chose them out of the world and that the Holy Spirit would help them testify about Him.

item.title: I Have Called You Friends
item.description: John 15:12-17 - Sitting with Jesus' words to His disciples shortly before His death, this reflection pauses over something remarkably personal: Jesus calls these men His friends. After years of living, traveling, and learning together, He reminds them that He chose them and invited them into a relationship marked by love, obedience, and closeness.

item.title: Connected to the Vine
item.description: John 15:1-11 - Jesus repeatedly invites His disciples to remain in Him, using the image of branches connected to a vine to show where life and fruitfulness come from. This reflection considers what it means to truly remain connected to Jesus—not merely to be among the branches—and the promise that as we abide in Him, He also makes His dwelling with us.

item.title: We Will Make Our Dwelling With Him
item.description: John 14:16-31 - Jesus continues to unfold the relationship between Himself, the Father, and the Holy Spirit, promising His disciples that He will not leave them as orphans. Rather than rushing through such a rich passage, this reflection sits with Jesus' repeated connection between loving Him and following His words—and the remarkable promise that God will make His dwelling with those who love Him.

item.title: Let Scripture Reveal Who God Is
item.description: John 14:7-15 - In a passage filled with deep theology, it can be easy to feel pressure to understand and explain everything at once. Slowing down to simply observe what Jesus says reveals something foundational: He is in the Father, the Father is in Him, and His words and works carry the Father's authority—inviting us to let Scripture itself shape our understanding of who God is.

item.title: What It Means to Believe
item.description: John 14:1-6 - Jesus tells His disciples not to let their hearts be troubled, but to believe in God and believe in Him. Looking more closely at the word believe reveals something deeper than simply accepting that something is true—it carries the idea of placing our trust in, relying on, and even casting ourselves upon God, especially when worry and uncertainty feel heavy.

item.title: Judas, Peter, and a New Commandment
item.description: John 13:21-38 - Some days in Scripture bring an immediate insight, and some days simply mean reading, noticing, and staying present with God's Word. Walking through Judas' betrayal, Jesus' command to love one another, and Peter's coming denial, this reflection is a reminder that time in Scripture is still worthwhile even when there isn't one clear application or lesson that jumps off the page.

item.title: He Loved Them to the End
item.description: John 13:1-20 - As the disciples argue over who is greatest, Jesus gives them a radically different picture of greatness by kneeling down and washing their feet. His actions reveal a love that chooses to serve humbly—even washing the feet of Judas, whom He knew would betray Him—and point toward the deeper cleansing He would soon provide through the cross.

item.title: Even If It Costs Everything
item.description: John 12:42-50 - Some of the rulers believed in Jesus but would not confess Him because they feared what following Him might cost. This reflection considers the difference between privately believing and being willing to live that belief openly, even when obedience may mean losing approval, relationships, or the life we once knew.

item.title: What Do We Do With the Thought?
item.description: John 12:27-41 - As Jesus faces what is coming, His soul is troubled—but He immediately brings that trouble to His Father and chooses the purpose He came to fulfill. This reflection considers the difference between having a thought, feeling, or temptation and what we choose to do with it, encouraging us to bring those moments to God rather than allowing them to take root and lead us somewhere they should not.

item.title: How to Use SOAP to Study Scripture
item.description: John 12:20-26 (John 12:24) - Stepping away from the usual reflection, this recording explains the SOAP method—Scripture, Observation, Application, and Prayer—and how it can help us slow down and listen for what God is showing us in His Word. The goal isn't a perfect study process, but simply to spend time with God, invite the Holy Spirit into the reading, and allow Scripture to work its way into everyday life.

item.title: Behold, Your King Is Coming
item.description: John 12:12-19 - John gives a remarkably simple account of Jesus' triumphal entry, drawing attention to fulfilled Scripture and to the testimony spreading after Lazarus was raised from the dead. Rather than rushing ahead to what comes next, this reflection pauses with John's continuing message: this is who Jesus is, and everything is unfolding according to God's timing.

item.title: Mary at the Feet of Jesus
item.description: John 12:1-11 - Across several moments in Mary's story, she is repeatedly found at the feet of Jesus—learning from Him, grieving before Him, and finally pouring out something extraordinarily costly in worship. Her story invites us to consider whether we are willing to keep returning to Jesus in every season: to learn, to grieve, and to give ourselves to Him in gratitude.

item.title: Alive, But Still Bound
item.description: John 11:38-46 - Lazarus walks out of the grave alive, but still wrapped in the burial cloths that had bound him. Reflecting on that image, Hope considers how Jesus calls us out of death into life—and how being made alive in Him does not mean we emerge instantly free from everything that once held us.

item.title: Jesus Meets Us in Our Grief
item.description: John 11:17-37 - Martha and Mary come to Jesus carrying the same loss, but He responds to each of them differently—meeting Martha with truth and hope, and Mary with compassion and tears. Even knowing that Lazarus would soon walk out of the grave, Jesus entered into their grief and met each sister exactly where she was.

item.title: Jesus and Psalm 82
item.description: John 10:22-42 - While reading John 10, Hope pauses at Jesus' quotation from Psalm 82 and follows the connection back into the Old Testament. The reflection explores what the phrase "you are gods" meant in context and highlights the way Jesus used Scripture to answer those questioning His identity.

item.title: Knowing the Shepherd's Voice
item.description: John 10:1-21 - Jesus describes Himself as the Good Shepherd whose sheep know and follow His voice. Reflecting on David's willingness to pursue and rescue his sheep, Hope considers both the Shepherd who faithfully comes after us and the kind of sheep she wants to become—one who recognizes His voice and eagerly follows rather than continually wandering away.

item.title: Are We Teachable?
item.description: John 9:35-41 - Jesus' words to the Pharisees raise a challenging question: are we teachable, or are we so certain of what we already believe that we cannot recognize truth when God puts it in front of us? This reflection considers what it looks like to invite the Holy Spirit into both Scripture and our circumstances, allowing Him to reveal what we may not yet see in our own hearts.
